raw.details:
Event Details:

  • Date: 22 October 2026
  • Time: 1:30 PM – 3:00 PM
  • Venue: NewGen IEDC FAB LAB, I.T.S Engineering College, Greater Noida
  • Registration Fee: ₹200 per team
  • Prize Pool: ₹8,000
  • Team Size: 2 participants per team

Event Description:

The Junior Makethon challenges school students to use their engineering creativity and resourcefulness to address the problem of modern-day waste generation. Using only scrap materials provided by the organizers, teams must transform waste into something useful or innovative — belonging to any category (civil, mechanical, electrical, artistic, or otherwise) — through upcycling.

Guidelines:

Eligibility & Team Composition:

  • Valid School ID is mandatory.
  • Both team members must work collaboratively to build the item within the given time.

Material Usage & Constraints:

  • Only scrap materials provided by the organizers may be used and must be repurposed into the final creation; permitted materials and tools will be announced at the venue.
  • Decorative or custom-made materials brought solely for aesthetic enhancement (paints, stickers, or any external items) are strictly prohibited.

Tools & Equipment:

  • Participants must bring their own basic construction tools (adhesives, tapes, scissors, and cutting tools).
  • Limited light workshop tools and safety equipment may be available at the venue, but teams should not rely on this.
  • Any provided workshop tool must be used with appropriate safety equipment and only under the direct supervision of an event coordinator.

Time Limit:

  • Suggested working duration: 90 minutes; the final duration will be confirmed and announced before the round begins.
  • Work begins only after the official start signal and must stop immediately once time expires.

Presentation:

After time is up, teams must present their creation to the judges, explaining:

  • Purpose: What the item is and how it can be used.
  • Concept: The idea and thought process behind its design.
  • Usefulness: Its practical application and utility.

Rules:

  • No participant may receive assistance from anyone outside their registered team.
  • Teams are expected to develop their own solutions; plagiarism or use of unauthorized external work may lead to disqualification.

Judging Criteria:

  • Innovation: 30%
  • Functionality: 30%
  • Resourcefulness: 20%
  • Presentation: 10%
  • Sustainability / Usefulness: 10%

Disqualification:

A team may be disqualified for:

  • Using materials other than the organizer-provided scrap (e.g., aesthetic add-ons).
  • Continuing work after the time limit expires.
  • Receiving outside assistance during the build.
  • Plagiarism or use of unauthorized pre-existing work.
  • Poor social conduct, misbehaviour, unsportsmanlike conduct, or failure to follow safety guidelines.
  • Failure to follow general tool-safety protocols while using workshop tools.

The judge's decision regarding final scores and any rule violations is final and binding.

Note: Registration fees are not refundable.
